newsitem.title: USA: Brazil wage ruling no threat to economy-US analyst.
newsitem.headline: Brazil wage ruling no threat to economy-US analyst.

text.p: Brazil's Supreme Court ruling on Wednesday to increase 11 civil servants' salaries by 28.9 percent will not pose a threat to the government's economic program, Morgan Stanley & Co economist Ernest Brown said in a report issued on Thursday.
"My initial impression is that the fiscal impact is not likely to derail the government's economic program," he said.
Brown said the high court's decision will not require major changes in his expectations for lower inflation and falling interest rates in Brazil.

Even if the constitutionally protected right for equal pay called "isonomia" were made fully applicable to all state employees, the cost would be 5.7 billion reals per year or 0.7 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP), he estimated.
As a result, the budget deficit would rise from 5.0 percent to 5.7 percent of GDP in 1997, and inflation would increase by one percentage point, Brown said.

The event, to be sure, is "a nuisance" for President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's administration as it complicates the monetary policy, but Brown contended that "there is nothing in this Supreme Court decree that melts down Brazil's anti-inflation program."
